_game: ViZDoom: Deadly Corridor (Doom action-shooter; COOM engine) -- full movement
_note: pip install vizdoom. Fight down a corridor to the vest at the end; enemies attack from side alcoves. Unlike DefendCenter this scenario HAS move buttons, so you can walk forward/back and strafe.
_keys_note: The env's action is MultiBinary over the scenario's buttons (env_kwargs.max_buttons_pressed 0), so 'keys' values are button indices in the scenario's available_buttons order -- VizdoomDeadlyCorridor-v1: 0=MOVE_LEFT, 1=MOVE_RIGHT, 2=ATTACK, 3=MOVE_FORWARD, 4=MOVE_BACKWARD, 5=TURN_LEFT, 6=TURN_RIGHT. Held keys combine (turn while shooting). The controls the subject sees are a plain 'message' phase; keep its text in sync with 'keys' by hand.
_audio_note: env_kwargs.audio_buffer_enabled turns Doom's sound on: it arrives in obs['audio'], is played through the session's speakers, and is logged per frame. Doom makes 1/35 s of sound per step, so fps * env_kwargs.frame_skip must be 35: the session stops the block otherwise, because sound could not follow the frames. This scenario used to run at fps 20, i.e. in slow motion; 35 is Doom's own tic rate, so the corridor now plays at the speed the scenario was designed for.
